sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin.
sentences.zh: 大家好，我是本杰明·普兰。

sentences.en: And I'm Mark Ronson.
sentences.zh: 我是马克·荣森。

sentences.en: And welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《重构者》，一档专注于设计之美及其周边文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl, every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you, and you turned a DJ booth
sentences.zh: 回想当年我在黑胶唱片时代去夜店当DJ的时候，每晚你都要带着300件你最珍爱的宝贝去上班，你把DJ台

sentences.en: into this, like, living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 变成了一个活生生的、充满美丽50年历史文物的快闪博物馆。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 欢迎在您喜爱的播客平台上收听来自爱彼的《重构者》。

sentences.en: We're entering the third week of illegal blockades that have been disrupting the lives of too many Canadians.
sentences.zh: 我们正在进入非法封锁的第三周，这些封锁已经扰乱了太多加拿大人正常的生活。

sentences.en: The federal government has invoked the Emergencies Act to supplement provincial and territorial capacity to address the blockades and occupations.
sentences.zh: 联邦政府已动用《紧急状态法》，以补充各省和地区应对封锁和占领的行政能力。

sentences.en: Invoking the Emergencies Act is never the first thing a government should do, nor even the second.
sentences.zh: 动用《紧急状态法》绝不是政府应当采取的首要手段，甚至连其次也算不上。

sentences.en: The act is to be used sparingly and as a last resort.
sentences.zh: 该法案必须审慎使用，作为最后手段。

sentences.en: I know that everyone is tired of this pandemic.
sentences.zh: 我知道大家都对这场大流行感到厌倦。

sentences.en: We're hearing your frustration with COVID and even with the temporary measures we had to put forward to keep people safe.
sentences.zh: 我们听到了你们对新冠疫情的不满，甚至对我们为保障人们安全而不得不推出的临时措施也有所怨言。

sentences.en: I know people are frustrated.
sentences.zh: 我知道大家都很沮丧。

sentences.en: I hear it.
sentences.zh: 我听到了。

sentences.en: You have a right to express that frustration and even your anger with the government or government policies.
sentences.zh: 你们有权表达这种沮丧，甚至是对政府或政府政策的愤怒。

sentences.en: It's something we'll always defend in this free and democratic country.
sentences.zh: 这是我们在这个自由民主国家将永远捍卫的权利。

sentences.en: But blockading streets and critical infrastructure and depriving your neighbors of their freedoms is a totally different thing.
sentences.zh: 但封锁街道和关键基础设施、剥夺邻居们的自由则是完全另一回事。

sentences.en: It has to stop.
sentences.zh: 这必须停止。

sentences.en: From the New York Times,
sentences.zh: 来自《纽约时报》，

sentences.en: I'm Michael Bavar.
sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴瓦尔。

sentences.en: This is a daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: For nearly three weeks now...
sentences.zh: 近三周来……

sentences.en: We begin the program in Canada where a standoff between truckers and the country's government over COVID restrictions shows no sign of ending.
sentences.zh: 我们从加拿大开始今天的节目，卡车司机与该国政府围绕新冠限制措施的对峙毫无结束的迹象。

sentences.en: Hundreds of truckers and their supporters have occupied Canada's capital city of Ottawa.
sentences.zh: 数百名卡车司机及其支持者占领了加拿大的首都渥太华。

sentences.en: The truckers are protesting Canada's mandate that requires them to be fully vaccinated against COVID or to quarantine.
sentences.zh: 卡车司机们正在抗议加拿大的强制令，该命令要求他们完全接种新冠疫苗才能入境，否则必须隔离。

sentences.en: In an unprecedented act of protest that has shocked the country's government.
sentences.zh: 这是一场震惊该国政府的史无前例的抗议行动。

sentences.en: Yesterday, for the first time in half a century,
sentences.zh: 昨天，半个世纪以来首次，

sentences.en: Canada's Prime Minister, Justin Trudeau, declared a national emergency, granting him enormous powers to intervene.
sentences.zh: 加拿大总理贾斯廷·特鲁多宣布进入国家紧急状态，赋予了他干预的巨大权力。

sentences.en: Today, I spoke with my colleague,
sentences.zh: 今天，我与我的同事、

sentences.en: Toronto Bureau Chief Catherine Porter, about a surprisingly American-seeming scene unfolding in Canada.
sentences.zh: 多伦多记者站主任凯瑟琳·波特进行了交谈，讨论了加拿大正在上演的一幕出奇带有美国风格的场景。

sentences.en: It's Wednesday, February 16th.
sentences.zh: 今天是2月16日，星期三。

sentences.en: Good morning, Catherine.
sentences.zh: 早上好，凯瑟琳。

sentences.en: Good morning, Michael.
sentences.zh: 早上好，迈克尔。

sentences.en: Nice to see you.
sentences.zh: 很高兴见到你。

sentences.en: Catherine, you look surprisingly rested and fresh for someone who has been out covering protests for a week.
sentences.zh: 凯瑟琳，对于一个出去采访抗议活动一周的人来说，你看上去出奇地精力充沛、神清气爽。

sentences.en: I'm not rested, but I am fresh.
sentences.zh: 我可不轻松，但我确实很清醒。

sentences.en: And I'm excited to talk to you.
sentences.zh: 而且我也很高兴能跟你聊聊。

sentences.en: Me too.
sentences.zh: 我也是。

sentences.en: So, Catherine, let's talk about how we got to this point, where the Prime Minister of Canada is now invoking emergency powers to end this standoff with protesters
sentences.zh: 那么，凯瑟琳，我们来谈谈事情是如何发展到这一步的：加拿大总理现在不得不动用紧急权力，来结束与抗议者在

sentences.en: in the country's capital.
sentences.zh: 国家首都的这场对峙。

sentences.en: Well, this started about a month ago.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这一切大约在一个月前就开始了。

sentences.en: There was a new law put in place that required truckers who cross the border into the United States to be vaccinated in order to come back across the border.
sentences.zh: 当时出台了一项新法律，要求跨越边境进入美国的卡车司机必须接种疫苗才能再次跨过边境返回。

sentences.en: Before then, that rule had not been something they had faced.
sentences.zh: 在此之前，他们从未面临过这样的规则。

sentences.en: And this was going to, for some of them who had not been vaccinated, threaten their livelihood.
sentences.zh: 对于其中一些尚未接种疫苗的人来说，这将威胁到他们的生计。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: So, this all begins with what's seen as an overly restrictive policy
sentences.zh: 所以，这一切都始于一项被视为过度限制的政策，

sentences.en: requiring that truckers get a vaccine.
sentences.zh: 即要求卡车司机接种疫苗。

sentences.en: In order to cross the international border and come back into Canada.
sentences.zh: 为了跨越国际边境并返回加拿大。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Overly restrictive.
sentences.zh: 过度限制。

sentences.en: Well, some of these truckers obviously felt so, but I think the reaction in a lot of Canada was kind of a shrug, because Canada's reaction to the pandemic,
sentences.zh: 好吧，其中一些卡车司机显然是这么认为的，但我认为加拿大大部分地区的反应有点像耸耸肩，因为加拿大对大流行的反应，

sentences.en: particularly as opposed to Americans' reaction, was to follow science, to lock everything down, and to get vaccinated as quickly as possible.
sentences.zh: 尤其是与美国人的反应相反，是遵循科学、封锁一切，并以最快速度接种疫苗。

sentences.en: We're now 85% of the population, five and up, has been double-vaxxed.
sentences.zh: 我们现在85%的五岁及以上人口已经接种了两剂疫苗。

sentences.en: We're one of the most vaccinated countries in the WeSt.
sentences.zh: 我们是西方疫苗接种率最高的国家之一。

sentences.en: We're also one of the strictest countries when it comes to restrictions.
sentences.zh: 在限制措施方面，我们也是最严厉的国家之一。

sentences.en: You know, it was only recently that Canada, or at least the part that I'm talking to you from, which is the biggest province here,
sentences.zh: 你知道的，直到最近，加拿大，或者至少是我正在跟你连线的这个地方——这里是加拿大最大的省份，

sentences.en: allowed indoor dining again.
sentences.zh: 才重新允许堂食。

sentences.en: And, you know, since the beginning of pandemic, it's only been a matter of months that they've allowed indoor dining.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，自大流行开始以来，他们允许堂食的时间也只有几个月而已。

sentences.en: It's almost entirely been either outside in Canada, imagine, or takeout.
sentences.zh: 在加拿大，几乎完全要么在室外，真敢想，要么就是外卖。

sentences.en: It's cold.
sentences.zh: 天气很冷。

sentences.en: It's very cold most of the, well, at least half the year is very cold.
sentences.zh: 大部分时间都很冷，好吧，至少有一半的时间非常冷。

sentences.en: You know, and my kids, I have two kids, and they have spent the majority of the last two years on a screen learning.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我的孩子们，我有两个孩子，他们过去两年中的大部分时间都在屏幕前学习。

sentences.en: In fact, the local papers repeat here that kids in Ontario have spent the least amount of time in classes, in classrooms, and anywhere in North America.
sentences.zh: 事实上，当地报纸在这里反复提到，安大略省的孩子们花在课堂上的时间是北美任何地方中最少的。

sentences.en: Wow, the whole continent.
sentences.zh: 哇，整个大陆都是如此。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So, the country's been under an extreme lockdown.
sentences.zh: 因此，这个国家一直处于极端的封锁之下。

sentences.en: But at the same time, you really haven't seen that pushback you've seen in the United States.
sentences.zh: 但与此同时，你确实没有看到在美国那种程度的抵制。

sentences.en: Polling has shown that consistently people support these type of strict public health measures to limit the spread of the virus.
sentences.zh: 民调显示，人们始终支持这种限制病毒传播的严格公共卫生措施。

sentences.en: You know, if anything, people here tend to criticize the government for not doing enough, not for what they're doing, but what they're not doing.
sentences.zh: 你知道，如果说有什么不同的话，那就是这里的人们往往会批评政府做得还不够，不是因为他们正在做的事，而是因为他们没有做的事。

sentences.en: And so, it's been a story of a largely compliant country where the national sentiment has been, let's take care of one another.
sentences.zh: 因此，这是一个高度顺从的国家的写照，其国民共识一直是：让我们照顾好彼此。

sentences.en: And that's something we're all going to do.
sentences.zh: 这是我们所有人都要做的事情。

sentences.en: We're in this together.
sentences.zh: 我们同舟共济。

sentences.en: So, you're saying ahead of this protest, not only were Canadians quite used to these kinds of policies and restrictions, they had been quite accepting of them.
sentences.zh: 所以你是说，在这次抗议之前，加拿大人不仅对这类政策和限制习以为常，而且一直相当接受它们。

sentences.en: It's like it's in the States.
sentences.zh: 这和美国的情况不一样。

sentences.en: It's not something that's pitted the political left versus the political right.
sentences.zh: 这并没有让政治左翼与政治右翼对立起来。

sentences.en: Even in the more conservative parts of the country, with conservative local governments, even there, they have mostly followed the science, followed public health experts,
sentences.zh: 即使在政治倾向更保守的地区、由保守派地方政府管辖的地方，甚至在那里，他们也大多遵循科学、听取公共卫生专家的意见，

sentences.en: and put down fairly stringent rules.
sentences.zh: 并制定了相当严格的规则。

sentences.en: And, you know, in cases where politicians have broken the rules, like, for instance, gone on vacation over Christmas when there was a lockdown in place,
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，在政客们违反规则的情况下，比如在实行封锁的圣诞节期间去度假，

sentences.en: the repercussions from the electorate have been severe, and they've lost cabinet positions over it.
sentences.zh: 选民的反弹是严厉的，他们因此失去了内阁职位。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: So, we should not understand this to be a story of more conservative, working-class Canadians
sentences.zh: 所以我们不应该把这理解为一个更加保守的工人阶级加拿大人

sentences.en: opposing this mandate on political grounds.
sentences.zh: 出于政治原因反对这一强制令的故事。

sentences.en: Well, you know, we could look at it through that lens now, but before this, I don't think that was the case at all.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道，我们现在或许可以透过这个角度来看待它，但在之前，我认为根本不是这样。

sentences.en: And I want to be clear, around 90% of truckers in Canada are vaccinated, according to the Canadian Truckers Alliance.
sentences.zh: 我想明确一点，根据加拿大卡车司机联盟的数据，加拿大约有90%的卡车司机接种了疫苗。

sentences.en: So, this is a small percentage of them.
sentences.zh: 所以这只是其中的一小部分人。

sentences.en: But for that group, they say that their livelihood is at stake, and they wanted to bring their beef to the capital and let it be known.
sentences.zh: 但对这群人来说，他们表示生计受到了威胁，因此他们想把不满带到首都并让外界知晓。

sentences.en: So, in January,
sentences.zh: 因此，在1月份，

sentences.en: a group of truckers and other organizers began what they called the Freedom Convoy, driving across the country, starting in the very far west towards the capital of Ottawa.
sentences.zh: 一群卡车司机和其他组织者发起了他们所谓的“自由车队”，驱车横跨全国，从最西端出发驶向首都渥太华。

sentences.en: Along the way, they get bigger and bigger.
sentences.zh: 一路上，他们的队伍越来越庞大。

sentences.en: And, you know, interestingly,
sentences.zh: 而且，有趣的是，

sentences.en: I'm talking to you right now from Toronto, which is the biggest city in Canada.
sentences.zh: 我现在正从多伦多——加拿大最大的城市——和你通话。

sentences.en: And people were, you know, lining the bridges like they normally do when the bodies of soldiers come back.
sentences.zh: 人们，你知道的，像平常阵亡士兵遗体运回时那样在桥两边排起长队。

sentences.en: People line the bridges to wave flags at the convoy of hearses, historically.
sentences.zh: 历史上，人们曾在桥两边排队向灵车车队挥舞旗帜。

sentences.en: But people were lining the bridges with Canadian flags, mostly with Canada flags, cheering them on.
sentences.zh: 但人们这次是在桥两边排起长队，挥舞着加拿大国旗，主要是加拿大国旗，为他们加油助威。

sentences.en: I believe in vaccinations.
sentences.zh: 我相信疫苗接种。

sentences.en: I'm not an anti-vaxxer, but enough is enough.
sentences.zh: 我不是反疫苗人士，但够了真是够了。

sentences.en: Our kids, my son, he's seven.
sentences.zh: 我们的孩子，我的儿子，他七岁了。

sentences.en: And all he talks about is he wants his childhood back.
sentences.zh: 他嘴里念叨的全部就是想要回他的童年。

sentences.en: He's sick of wearing a mask at school.
sentences.zh: 他厌倦了在学校戴口罩。

sentences.en: He cries to go to school.
sentences.zh: 他哭着不想去学校。

sentences.en: But he loves school.
sentences.zh: 但他很爱学校。

sentences.en: So, you know, I want my Canada back.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，我想要回我的加拿大。

sentences.en: I want freedom.
sentences.zh: 我想要自由。

sentences.en: These weren't huge crowds of people, but there were crowds of people.
sentences.zh: 这些虽然不是庞大的人群，但确实有人群聚集。

sentences.en: So there was evidence along the way that they had tapped into something.
sentences.zh: 因此一路上有迹象表明，他们触动了某种东西。

sentences.en: You know, it wasn't just about the truckers.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这不仅仅关乎卡车司机。

sentences.en: It wasn't just about their jobs.
sentences.zh: 这不仅仅关乎他们的工作。

sentences.en: They had tapped into an undercurrent in Canada of frustration.
sentences.zh: 他们触动了加拿大潜藏的挫败感暗流。

sentences.en: So what happens, Catherine, when this freedom convoy arrives in the capital, in Ottawa?
sentences.zh: 那么，凯瑟琳，当这个自由车队抵达首都渥太华时，发生了什么？

sentences.en: So first you need to know
sentences.zh: 所以首先你需要知道，

sentences.en: Ottawa is this sleepy capital of Canada.
sentences.zh: 渥太华是加拿大这样一个沉睡的首都。

sentences.en: It's generally a small city full of bureaucrats and politicians who fly in for business.
sentences.zh: 它通常是个小城市，到处都是来这里出差的官僚和政客。

sentences.en: One thing that it's used to, though, is proteSt.
sentences.zh: 不过，它习惯了一件事，那就是抗议。

sentences.en: There's lots of protests, just like in Washington.
sentences.zh: 这里有大量的抗议活动，就像华盛顿一样。

sentences.en: So the fact that these guys come in doesn't take anyone by surprise.
sentences.zh: 所以这些人进来并没有让任何人感到意外。

sentences.en: They roar into the city and they end up on the street, really in the political heart of the country, right in front of the legislature, beside the prime minister's office,
sentences.zh: 他们轰鸣着驶入这座城市，最终停在了街上，真正进入了国家的政治核心区，就在议会大厦前、总理办公室旁、

sentences.en: all of the elected representatives' offices, the Supreme Court.
sentences.zh: 所有民选代表的办公室以及最高法院旁边。

sentences.en: And they line up their trucks along the street and onto many of the side streets and they begin to proteSt.
sentences.zh: 他们把卡车一字排开停在街上以及许多小巷里，并开始抗议。

sentences.en: What I think surprised people was that I do know from local politicians that they had been briefed by the police and they thought,
sentences.zh: 我认为让大家感到惊讶的是，我确实从当地政客那里了解到，他们曾听取过警察的简报，并且他们以为，

sentences.en: OK, these guys are going to come.
sentences.zh: 好吧，这些人会来。

sentences.en: They're going to make a lot of noise.
sentences.zh: 他们会制造很多噪音。

sentences.en: It's going to be a typical boisterous proteSt.
sentences.zh: 这将是一场典型的喧闹抗议。

sentences.en: They'll be here for a day or two, probably for the weekend.
sentences.zh: 他们会在这里呆上一两天，大概就是个周末。

sentences.en: And come Monday, they will roar out of town the same way that they roared in, having made their point.
sentences.zh: 到了周一，他们就会像轰鸣着进城那样，轰鸣着离开小镇，表明他们的观点。

sentences.en: And what happened on Monday?
sentences.zh: 那周一发生了什么？

sentences.en: They stayed.
sentences.zh: 他们留了下来。

sentences.en: And they kept honking.
sentences.zh: 他们一直在按喇叭。

sentences.en: And they are allowed to stay for some reason.
sentences.zh: 而且不知出于什么原因，他们被允许留下来。

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, I think a big debate went on is still continuing to go on as to why the police did not try and move them.
sentences.zh: 对，我的意思是，我认为此前发生过一场激烈的辩论，并且现在仍在继续，关于为什么警方没有试图驱逐他们。

sentences.en: But I think the biggest innovation of this protest, the thing that took everyone by surprise is you can move a bunch of protesters who are on foot,
sentences.zh: 但我认为这次抗议最大的创新、让所有人感到意外的是，你可以驱散一群步行的抗议者，

sentences.en: but moving a 30,000-pound tractor trailer
sentences.zh: 但要移动一辆重达3万磅的半挂式卡车

sentences.en: takes something quite different.
sentences.zh: 需要完全不同的手段。

sentences.en: So these guys had moved in with these brilliant protest machines because they're super heavy.
sentences.zh: 所以这些家伙开着这些绝妙的抗议机器进驻，因为它们超级重。

sentences.en: You know, they're really hard to move.
sentences.zh: 你知道，它们真的很难移动。

sentences.en: I talked to tow truck operators who told me that it takes an hour just to hook one of these things up, let alone move it.
sentences.zh: 我跟拖车司机聊过，他们告诉我，光是把其中一辆车挂钩就得花一个小时，更不用说挪动它了。

sentences.en: They come with really big noise-making machines that are, like, meant to tell the moose and whatever else is on the highway to get out of the way.
